info.title: Ignition HTTP API
info.description:
### About this page
This specification covers all public HTTP API endpoints for the Ignition platform and currently
installed modules. It is intended to be used by developers to understand the capabilities and
data formats used by the API. This documentation is generated from the
[OpenAPI](https://www.openapis.org/) specification document which is available in JSON format
[here](/openapi.json).

post.description: Generates a key and hash pair suitable for a new API Token. Clients should store the key somewhere safe, such as a password manager or secrets manager. The key is the credential that the client will include with each request for authentication purposes. The hash is a secure digest of the key and should be sent to Ignition as the token hash when creating a new API key. WARNING: it is strongly recommended to call this API using https, otherwise the security of the token could be compromised.

200.description: Success. Returns a JSON encoding of the generated API Token.

key.title: Key
key.description: The raw API key that the client will include with each request for authentication purposes. Clients should store the key somewhere safe, such as a password manager or secrets manager.

hash.title: Hash
hash.description: A secure digest of the key which should be sent to Ignition as the token hash when creating a new API Token. Clients can safely discard this value once a new API Token is created with this hash.

403.description: The request does not have the required write permissions.

500.description: A server error occurred while trying to generate the API Token.

get.description: Generates a *.gwbk file that can be downloaded.

parameters.name: includePeerLocal
parameters.description:
In a redundant gateway environment, set this parameter to 'true' to retrieve local-specific files from the
redundant peer over the gateway network. These files will be stored in the .gwbk alongside the local-specific
files from this gateway.

500.description: A server error occurred while creating the .gwbk file

post.description: Processes and restores a *.gwbk file on this gateway. The gateway will then be restarted.

parameters.name: restoreDisabled
parameters.description: If `true`, all projects, database connections, OPC connections, etc will be disabled upon restart. Default is `false`

parameters.name: disableTempProjectBackup
parameters.description: If `true`, the projects dir will not have a temporary backup created during the restore process. Default is `false`

parameters.name: renameEnabled
parameters.description: If `true` will allow overriding the name of the gateway before it is restored. Default is `false`

parameters.name: newName
parameters.description: The new gateway name to use on restore.

parameters.name: restoreLocal
parameters.description:
Set this parameter to `true` to restore local-specific files on the gateway. These files will be restored to the
data/config/local folder and the data/config/resources/local folder. Note that existing files in these folders
will be deleted. Default value is `false`.

requestBody.description: The contents of the *.gwbk file as a stream of bytes.

400.description: The .gwbk is from an Ignition version that cannot be restored in this gateway, or the .gwbk does not contain a valid version.

403.description: Gateway restoration is not allowed against a redundant backup gateway.

500.description: A server occurred when attempting to apply the restoration file.

get.description: Information on the current status of the redundancy system.
The configuration of the redundancy system. Note that the gatewayNetworkSetup section only applies to the redundant backup.

gatewayNetworkSetup.description: Gateway network settings to establish a connection to the redundant master.

host.description: The address of the master gateway.

port.description: The Gateway Network port of the master gateway.

enableSsl.description: Whether to use SSL to connect to the master gateway.

pingRate.description: How often, in milliseconds, to send a ping to the master.

pingTimeout.description: The maximum time, in milliseconds, allowed for a ping response. Pings that time out are counted as missed pings.

pingMaxMissed.description: The amount of missed pings that will force the connection to the master to be considered faulted.

websocketTimeout.description: The maximum time, in milliseconds, allowed for a new web socket to connect to the master.

httpConnectTimeout.description: The maximum time, in milliseconds, allowed to establish an HTTP connection to the master.

httpReadTimeout.description: The maximum time, in milliseconds, allowed to read or send HTTP data to the master.

sendThreads.description: Number of threads to use for sending messages.

receiveThreads.description: Number of threads to use for receiving messages.

activeHistoryLevel.description: If Partial, history will be cached instead of stored while the master is down. After the master and the backup reconnect, the cached history data will be compared to the master's stored history data to  eliminate data overlaps from being stored.

joinWaitTime.description: The time in milliseconds that the system will wait at startup for the other redundant node to connect. If this time is exceeded without establishing contact, this node will become active regardless of node role.

role.description: Enable or disable redundancy, and specify this node's role.

standbyActivityLevel.description: If set to Warm, the backup node will establish subscriptions to other systems such as OPC-UA. These subscriptions will remain inert until the node becomes active. Using the Warm setting can help reduce failover time.

syncTimeoutSecs.description: The maximum time (in seconds) allowed for a redundancy sync operation. Sync operations that exceed this value will time out.

autoDetectLocal.description: If true, the system will automatically detect which network interface to use. Most commonly disabled on systems with multiple network cards, in order to explicitly specify which interface to use.

localInterface.description: The IP address of the network interface to use for redundancy. Only used if auto-detect is turned off.

masterRecoveryMode.description: When set to Manual, the backup node will remain active after reconnecting to the master. A failover operation must be manually initiated on the gateway redundancy page for the master to become active again.

useActiveUptimeToResolveConflict.description: When a redundancy data conflict is detected between the master and the backup, and this setting is enabled, the systems will compare which has been running longer. Data from the longer running system will be used, and data from the other system will be discarded.

requestBody.description: A json object containing the new redundancy configuration

parameters.name: allowInvalidReferences
parameters.description: If true, invalid references will be allowed. Default is false.

collection.description: The config collection to modify the resource in

enabled.description: Whether the resource should be enabled

type.description: Type code of the extension point.

settings.description: Type-specific settings, if applicable. Object schema will change based upon extension point type.

partitionInterval.description: The partition interval used when creating tables.

dataDeduplication.description: When deduplication is enabled, incoming data with matching keys will update existing entries rather than create new ones, which helps maintain data integrity by allowing corrected data to replace erroneous entries.

maintenanceSettings.description: Specifies the maintenance settings for handling data that exceeds the retention limit.

strategy.description: Determines whether older data is archived to a target location or permanently deleted.

directory.description: Specifies the target directory path where data will be archived when maintenance mode is set to ARCHIVE. Must be a valid, writable directory location.

maintenanceAge.description: Specifies the age threshold for data maintenance.

filePath.description: Specifies the CSV file path. Required format: timestamp column followed by value columns, with tag names defined in the header row.

relativeTimestamps.description: When enabled, treats the first timestamp as a reference point, interpreting subsequent timestamps as relative offsets from this initial time.

progId.description: Each OPC server is identified by a "progid". This is the name that will be used to connect to the server.

isRemote.description: If selected, DCOM will be used to connect to the server on the specified Host with the given ProgId or CLSID.

host.description: The name or IP address of the machine hosting the server. Leave empty for local machine.

clsid.description: The CLSID of the server. If not specified, will be obtained using the ProgId.

flatBrowse.description: Flat browsing returns all items at once. This is less efficient than normal browsing, but if a server only supports flat browsing, select this option.

primaryHistorian.description: The primary historian for data storage and queries. Serves as the default query source unless limited by time constraints or when unavailable.

secondaryHistorian.description: The secondary historian for data storage, handling queries when the primary is unavailable or when queries exceed the configured time limit.

queryLimit.description: Controls whether queries are routed based on time constraints.

enabled.description: If enabled, older queries are automatically directed to the secondary historian.

size.description: Specifies how far back in time queries will be handled by the primary historian before routing to the secondary historian.

units.description: The time unit used for the query routing threshold.

timeLimit.description: Controls whether data is retained based on age.

enabled.description: If enabled, older data is removed to maintain the specified time limit.

size.description: Specifies how long data should be retained before removal.

sizeUnits.description: The time unit used for the storage time limit.

pointLimit.description: Controls whether data is limited by the total number of stored points.

enabled.description: If enabled, oldest points are removed when limit is exceeded.

size.description: Specifies the maximum number of data points to retain in storage.

remoteSync.description: Configures real-time data synchronization to a remote gateway historian.

enabled.description: If enabled, historical data is synchronized based on the specified frequency, batch size, and optional schedule constraints.

serverName.description: The target Gateway for remote synchronization. Must have the Historian Core module installed and allow remote storage.

historianName.description: The historian on the remote gateway where data will be synchronized.

enableSchedule.description: When enabled, data synchronization only occurs during the specified time ranges.

schedule.description: Defines when synchronization is allowed using time ranges in 24-hour format. Examples: "9:00-15:00", "21:00-05:00", "20:30-04:30". Use comma-separation for multiple ranges.

syncFrequencySize.description: Specifies the interval between data synchronization attempts to the remote gateway. Works in conjunction with the sync schedule when enabled.

syncFrequencyUnits.description: The time unit used for the sync frequency.

maxBatchSize.description: The maximum number of data points included in each synchronization transmission to the remote gateway.

serverName.description: Specifies the gateway used to connect to the remote historian.

historianName.description: Specifies the target remote historian for data operations.

storageAllowed.description: Specifies whether the provider operates in read-only or storage mode. When enabled, creates a store-forward engine to forward data to the remote gateway. When disabled, only supports historical data queries.

maxGroupSize.description: Specifies the maximum number of data points per transmission request in storage mode. Set to 0 for unlimited batch size.

database.description: Specifies the target SQL database for storing and retrieving historical data.

partition.description: Configures how data is segmented into time-based partitions.

enabled.description: Enables time-based table partitioning to segment historical data. Partitioning improves query performance and simplifies data lifecycle management.

size.description: Specifies the time duration of each partition, using the defined time unit.

sizeUnits.description: Specifies the time unit used to define partition duration.

partitionSeedQueryLimit.description: The maximum number of past partitions the SQL historian system will look through to find a seed value. A value of 0 will globally disable seed queries, a negative number will search every available partition

optimized.description: Enables data pre-processing within partitions to optimize query performance. While consuming additional storage space, this feature reduces query time by maintaining summarized data.

optimizedWindowSeconds.description: Specifies the time interval used for data summarization when partition optimization is enabled.

pruning.description: Configures data pruning by specifying the age threshold and time units for determining when historical data becomes eligible for deletion at the partition level.

enabled.description: Enables periodic pruning of older partitions.

age.description: Specifies the age threshold for data retention.

ageUnits.description: Specifies the time unit used for the data retention age threshold.

trackSce.description: Controls quality validation for calculated values based on tag group execution status. When enabled, values are marked as bad quality if calculated outside their tag group's execution period. When disabled, values inherit the tag's latest quality state.

staleMultiplier.description: Defines the staleness threshold as a multiple of the tag group execution rate. Values are marked as bad quality when the time since last recorded execution exceeds this threshold.

datasource.description: Specifies the target SQL database for querying historical data.

staleMultiplier.description: Defines the staleness threshold as a multiple of the tag group execution rate. Values are marked as bad quality when the time since last recorded execution exceeds this threshold.

datasource.description: Specifies the target SQL database for querying historical data.

type.description: Type code of the extension point.

settings.description: Type-specific settings, if applicable. Object schema will change based upon extension point type.

partitionInterval.description: The partition interval used when creating tables.

dataDeduplication.description: When deduplication is enabled, incoming data with matching keys will update existing entries rather than create new ones, which helps maintain data integrity by allowing corrected data to replace erroneous entries.

maintenanceSettings.description: Specifies the maintenance settings for handling data that exceeds the retention limit.

strategy.description: Determines whether older data is archived to a target location or permanently deleted.

directory.description: Specifies the target directory path where data will be archived when maintenance mode is set to ARCHIVE. Must be a valid, writable directory location.

maintenanceAge.description: Specifies the age threshold for data maintenance.

filePath.description: Specifies the CSV file path. Required format: timestamp column followed by value columns, with tag names defined in the header row.

relativeTimestamps.description: When enabled, treats the first timestamp as a reference point, interpreting subsequent timestamps as relative offsets from this initial time.

progId.description: Each OPC server is identified by a "progid". This is the name that will be used to connect to the server.

isRemote.description: If selected, DCOM will be used to connect to the server on the specified Host with the given ProgId or CLSID.

host.description: The name or IP address of the machine hosting the server. Leave empty for local machine.

clsid.description: The CLSID of the server. If not specified, will be obtained using the ProgId.

flatBrowse.description: Flat browsing returns all items at once. This is less efficient than normal browsing, but if a server only supports flat browsing, select this option.

primaryHistorian.description: The primary historian for data storage and queries. Serves as the default query source unless limited by time constraints or when unavailable.

secondaryHistorian.description: The secondary historian for data storage, handling queries when the primary is unavailable or when queries exceed the configured time limit.

queryLimit.description: Controls whether queries are routed based on time constraints.

enabled.description: If enabled, older queries are automatically directed to the secondary historian.

size.description: Specifies how far back in time queries will be handled by the primary historian before routing to the secondary historian.

units.description: The time unit used for the query routing threshold.

timeLimit.description: Controls whether data is retained based on age.

enabled.description: If enabled, older data is removed to maintain the specified time limit.

size.description: Specifies how long data should be retained before removal.

sizeUnits.description: The time unit used for the storage time limit.

pointLimit.description: Controls whether data is limited by the total number of stored points.

enabled.description: If enabled, oldest points are removed when limit is exceeded.

size.description: Specifies the maximum number of data points to retain in storage.

remoteSync.description: Configures real-time data synchronization to a remote gateway historian.

enabled.description: If enabled, historical data is synchronized based on the specified frequency, batch size, and optional schedule constraints.

serverName.description: The target Gateway for remote synchronization. Must have the Historian Core module installed and allow remote storage.

historianName.description: The historian on the remote gateway where data will be synchronized.

enableSchedule.description: When enabled, data synchronization only occurs during the specified time ranges.

schedule.description: Defines when synchronization is allowed using time ranges in 24-hour format. Examples: "9:00-15:00", "21:00-05:00", "20:30-04:30". Use comma-separation for multiple ranges.

syncFrequencySize.description: Specifies the interval between data synchronization attempts to the remote gateway. Works in conjunction with the sync schedule when enabled.

syncFrequencyUnits.description: The time unit used for the sync frequency.

maxBatchSize.description: The maximum number of data points included in each synchronization transmission to the remote gateway.

serverName.description: Specifies the gateway used to connect to the remote historian.

historianName.description: Specifies the target remote historian for data operations.

storageAllowed.description: Specifies whether the provider operates in read-only or storage mode. When enabled, creates a store-forward engine to forward data to the remote gateway. When disabled, only supports historical data queries.

maxGroupSize.description: Specifies the maximum number of data points per transmission request in storage mode. Set to 0 for unlimited batch size.

database.description: Specifies the target SQL database for storing and retrieving historical data.

partition.description: Configures how data is segmented into time-based partitions.

enabled.description: Enables time-based table partitioning to segment historical data. Partitioning improves query performance and simplifies data lifecycle management.

size.description: Specifies the time duration of each partition, using the defined time unit.

sizeUnits.description: Specifies the time unit used to define partition duration.

partitionSeedQueryLimit.description: The maximum number of past partitions the SQL historian system will look through to find a seed value. A value of 0 will globally disable seed queries, a negative number will search every available partition

optimized.description: Enables data pre-processing within partitions to optimize query performance. While consuming additional storage space, this feature reduces query time by maintaining summarized data.

optimizedWindowSeconds.description: Specifies the time interval used for data summarization when partition optimization is enabled.

pruning.description: Configures data pruning by specifying the age threshold and time units for determining when historical data becomes eligible for deletion at the partition level.

enabled.description: Enables periodic pruning of older partitions.

age.description: Specifies the age threshold for data retention.

ageUnits.description: Specifies the time unit used for the data retention age threshold.

trackSce.description: Controls quality validation for calculated values based on tag group execution status. When enabled, values are marked as bad quality if calculated outside their tag group's execution period. When disabled, values inherit the tag's latest quality state.

staleMultiplier.description: Defines the staleness threshold as a multiple of the tag group execution rate. Values are marked as bad quality when the time since last recorded execution exceeds this threshold.

datasource.description: Specifies the target SQL database for querying historical data.

put.description: Modify one or more Call Script resources

collection.description: The config collection to modify the resource in

enabled.description: Whether the resource should be enabled

greeting.description: The initial greeting message for the notification.
greeting.title: Greeting
greeting.default: Hello, this is an Ignition alarm notification.

challenge.description: A message asking the user to enter their PIN number. Must instruct them to press '#' when finished.
challenge.title: PIN Challenge
challenge.default: Please enter your pin, followed by the pound sign.

nonChallenge.description: When a PIN is not required, this message is played to instruct the users to press any key to continue.
nonChallenge.title: Non-PIN Challenge
nonChallenge.default: Please press any key to continue.

invalidPin.description: The message to play when a user enters the wrong PIN number.
invalidPin.title: Invalid PIN

summary.description: When there are multiple alarms, this message will be played to tell the user how many to expect. It must include the placeholder '%d' somewhere in the message.
summary.title: Summary

activeMessage.description: The message to play for active alarms. This message can reference properties of alarms by using syntax like "{propertyName}".
activeMessage.title: Active Message
activeMessage.default: At {eventTime|hh:mm:ss}, alarm named {name} became {eventState} with a value of {eventValue}

clearMessage.description: The message to play for cleared alarms. This message can reference properties of alarms by using syntax like "{propertyName}".
clearMessage.title: Clear Message
clearMessage.default: At {eventTime|hh:mm:ss}, alarm named {name} became {eventState} with a value of {eventValue}

option1.description: Tells the user to press '1' to acknowledge.
option1.title: Option 1: Acknowledge

ackConf.description: Tells the user that the alarm event has been successfully acknowledged.
ackConf.title: Acknowledge Confirmation

option2.description: Tells the user to press '2' to ignore/bypass the alarm.
option2.title: Option 2: Ignore

ignoreConf.description: When a user chooses to ignore the alarm notification, this message is played.
ignoreConf.title: Ignore Confirmation

option3.description: Tells the user to press '3' to repeat the last message.
option3.title: Option 3: Repeat

closing.description: The final message to play for the user before ending the call.
closing.title: Closing

username.description: Only used when Use SMTP Profile is false.

ciphertext.title: JWE Ciphertext

directory.description: Specifies the target directory path where data will be archived when maintenance mode is set to ARCHIVE. Must be a valid, writable directory location.

maintenanceAge.description: Specifies the age threshold for data maintenance.

filePath.description: Specifies the CSV file path. Required format: timestamp column followed by value columns, with tag names defined in the header row.

relativeTimestamps.description: When enabled, treats the first timestamp as a reference point, interpreting subsequent timestamps as relative offsets from this initial time.

progId.description: Each OPC server is identified by a "progid". This is the name that will be used to connect to the server.

isRemote.description: If selected, DCOM will be used to connect to the server on the specified Host with the given ProgId or CLSID.

host.description: The name or IP address of the machine hosting the server. Leave empty for local machine.

clsid.description: The CLSID of the server. If not specified, will be obtained using the ProgId.

flatBrowse.description: Flat browsing returns all items at once. This is less efficient than normal browsing, but if a server only supports flat browsing, select this option.

primaryHistorian.description: The primary historian for data storage and queries. Serves as the default query source unless limited by time constraints or when unavailable.

secondaryHistorian.description: The secondary historian for data storage, handling queries when the primary is unavailable or when queries exceed the configured time limit.

queryLimit.description: Controls whether queries are routed based on time constraints.

enabled.description: If enabled, older queries are automatically directed to the secondary historian.

size.description: Specifies how far back in time queries will be handled by the primary historian before routing to the secondary historian.

units.description: The time unit used for the query routing threshold.

timeLimit.description: Controls whether data is retained based on age.

enabled.description: If enabled, older data is removed to maintain the specified time limit.

size.description: Specifies how long data should be retained before removal.

sizeUnits.description: The time unit used for the storage time limit.

pointLimit.description: Controls whether data is limited by the total number of stored points.

enabled.description: If enabled, oldest points are removed when limit is exceeded.

size.description: Specifies the maximum number of data points to retain in storage.

remoteSync.description: Configures real-time data synchronization to a remote gateway historian.

enabled.description: If enabled, historical data is synchronized based on the specified frequency, batch size, and optional schedule constraints.

serverName.description: The target Gateway for remote synchronization. Must have the Historian Core module installed and allow remote storage.

historianName.description: The historian on the remote gateway where data will be synchronized.

enableSchedule.description: When enabled, data synchronization only occurs during the specified time ranges.

schedule.description: Defines when synchronization is allowed using time ranges in 24-hour format. Examples: "9:00-15:00", "21:00-05:00", "20:30-04:30". Use comma-separation for multiple ranges.

syncFrequencySize.description: Specifies the interval between data synchronization attempts to the remote gateway. Works in conjunction with the sync schedule when enabled.

syncFrequencyUnits.description: The time unit used for the sync frequency.

maxBatchSize.description: The maximum number of data points included in each synchronization transmission to the remote gateway.

serverName.description: Specifies the gateway used to connect to the remote historian.

historianName.description: Specifies the target remote historian for data operations.

storageAllowed.description: Specifies whether the provider operates in read-only or storage mode. When enabled, creates a store-forward engine to forward data to the remote gateway. When disabled, only supports historical data queries.

maxGroupSize.description: Specifies the maximum number of data points per transmission request in storage mode. Set to 0 for unlimited batch size.

database.description: Specifies the target SQL database for storing and retrieving historical data.

partition.description: Configures how data is segmented into time-based partitions.

enabled.description: Enables time-based table partitioning to segment historical data. Partitioning improves query performance and simplifies data lifecycle management.

size.description: Specifies the time duration of each partition, using the defined time unit.

sizeUnits.description: Specifies the time unit used to define partition duration.

partitionSeedQueryLimit.description: The maximum number of past partitions the SQL historian system will look through to find a seed value. A value of 0 will globally disable seed queries, a negative number will search every available partition

optimized.description: Enables data pre-processing within partitions to optimize query performance. While consuming additional storage space, this feature reduces query time by maintaining summarized data.

optimizedWindowSeconds.description: Specifies the time interval used for data summarization when partition optimization is enabled.

pruning.description: Configures data pruning by specifying the age threshold and time units for determining when historical data becomes eligible for deletion at the partition level.

enabled.description: Enables periodic pruning of older partitions.

age.description: Specifies the age threshold for data retention.

ageUnits.description: Specifies the time unit used for the data retention age threshold.

trackSce.description: Controls quality validation for calculated values based on tag group execution status. When enabled, values are marked as bad quality if calculated outside their tag group's execution period. When disabled, values inherit the tag's latest quality state.

staleMultiplier.description: Defines the staleness threshold as a multiple of the tag group execution rate. Values are marked as bad quality when the time since last recorded execution exceeds this threshold.

datasource.description: Specifies the target SQL database for querying historical data.

type.description: Type code of the extension point.

settings.description: Type-specific settings, if applicable. Object schema will change based upon extension point type.

partitionInterval.description: The partition interval used when creating tables.

dataDeduplication.description: When deduplication is enabled, incoming data with matching keys will update existing entries rather than create new ones, which helps maintain data integrity by allowing corrected data to replace erroneous entries.

x5u.description: The "x5u" (X.509 URL) parameter is a URI [RFC3986] that refers to a resource for an X.509 public key certificate or certificate chain [RFC5280]. The identified resource MUST provide a representation of the certificate or certificate chain that conforms to RFC 5280 in PEM-encoded form, with each certificate delimited as specified in Section 6.1 of RFC 4945. The key in the first certificate MUST match the public key represented by other members of the JWK.

x5c.title: X.509 Certificate Chain
x5c.description: The "x5c" (X.509 certificate chain) parameter contains a chain of one or more PKIX certificates [RFC5280]. The certificate chain is represented as a JSON array of certificate value strings. Each string in the array is a base64-encoded (Section 4 of [RFC4648] -- not base64url-encoded) DER [ITU.X690.1994] PKIX certificate value.The PKIX certificate containing the key value MUST be the first certificate. This MAY be followed by additional certificates, with each subsequent certificate being the one used to certify the previous one. The key in the first certificate MUST match the public key represented by other members of the JWK.

x5t.title: X.509 Certificate SHA-1 Thumbprint

x5t#S256.title: X.509 Certificate SHA-256 Thumbprint

userPrefix.description: This prefix will be prepended to the username before an Active Directory bind is attempted for authentication.

userSuffix.description: This suffix will be appended to the username before an Active Directory bind is attempted for authentication.

automaticSuffix.description: If this option is checked, and the suffix is left blank, then the suffix will automatically be assigned a value of "@<domain>"

usePrefixAndSuffixForGatewayUser.description: If this option is checked, the username prefix and suffix will be applied to the Gateway username before a bind is attempted.

userSearchBase.description: The base folder to search for users under, such as: DC=MyCompany,DC=com. The entire subtree under this folder will be searched using the User Search Filter. Multiple subtrees can be specified by putting them in parentheses, like so: (OU=Administrators,DC=MyCompany,DC=com)(OU=Operators,DC=MyCompany,DC=com). If you leave this blank the whole subtree of the domain controller will be searched.

userSearchFilter.description: The LDAP search filter to use to find a specific user. Use the placeholder {0} as a standin for the login name.

userListFilter.description: The LDAP search filter used when querying for the list of all users. Should restrict the type to user.

userNameAttribute.description: The attribute on the User object to define the username.

userIdAttribute.description: The attribute on the User object to define the user's unique ID.

name.description: The name used to look up the attribute in LDAP.

binary.description: Treat the LDAP attribute's value as a byte[] array instead of as a String.

userRoleAttribute.description: Attributes of this name on the User object will define the user's roles.

nestedGroups.description: If this option is checked, nested group membership lookups will be performed.

groupRoleAttribute.description: Attributes of this name on the Group object will define the group's roles. This setting is only applicable when nested group membership is enabled.

roleNameAttribute.description: The attribute of this name on the Role object will define the role's name. Leave blank to use the raw value of the attribute defined by User Role Attribute.

roleIdAttribute.description: The attribute of this name on the Role object will define the role's unique ID.

name.description: The name used to look up the attribute in LDAP.

binary.description: Treat the LDAP attribute's value as a byte[] array instead of as a String.

phoneAttribute.description: The attribute name on the user object that represents the user's phone number

emailAttribute.description: The attribute name on the user object that represents the user's email address

smsAttribute.description: The attribute name on the user object that represents the phone number that this user receives text messages on.

badgeAttribute.description: The attribute on the User object to define the badge. This setting is required to enable badge-based authentication.

connectTimeout.description: The connection timeout in milliseconds for LDAP operations. No value or a value of less than one means the underlying network protocol's timeout will be used.

readTimeout.description: The read timeout in milliseconds for LDAP operations.

pageSize.description: The number of entries returned per page of results in a query

roleSearchBase.description: The base folder to search for roles under, such as: OU=Roles,DC=MyCompany,DC=com. The entire subtree under this folder will be searched using the Role Search Filter. If you specify the root of your tree structure, the search may take a very long time. Multiple subtrees can be specified by putting them in parentheses, like so: (OU=Builtin,DC=MyCompany,DC=com)(OU=Users,DC=MyCompany,DC=com). If you leave this blank the whole subtree of the domain controller will be searched.

roleSearchFilter.description: The LDAP search filter to use to locate roles.

badgeSearchFilter.description: The LDAP search filter to use to find a specific user given a badge. Use the placeholder {0} as a standin for the user's badge. Example: (&(objectClass=user)(badge={0}))

allowAnon.description:
If enabled, authentication attempts with blank passwords will be passed through to LDAP, which may choose to accept them.

WARNING: it is highly recommended to disable this setting unless you know it is required. AD servers may allow logging in as any user with a blank password when Security Authentication is set to “None” or “Simple” (even if a provided username does not exist in AD), which is a major security risk.

securityProtocol.description: The security protocol to use when connecting to the LDAP server. AUTO will attempt to use the most secure protocol available.

authenticationType.description: The authentication type to use when connecting to the LDAP server. AUTO will attempt to use the most secure authentication type available.

saslMechanism.description: An ordered list of space-separated mechanism names. The LDAP provider will use the first mechanism for which it finds an implementation. A blank value will leave this setting unspecified.

saslRealm.description: A realm defines the namespace from which the user is selected. A blank value will leave this setting unspecified. It is highly recommended to set the target realm otherwise any available realm may be chosen. This setting will only be used by mechanisms which support it.

saslQualityOfProtection.description: A comma-separated list of Quality-of-Protection (QoP) values, the order of which specifies the preference order. There are three well-known values: "auth" (authentication only), "auth-int" (authentication with integrity protection), and "auth-conf" (authentication with integrity and privacy protection). A blank value will leave this setting unspecified. This setting will only be used by mechanisms which support it.

saslProtectionStrength.description: A comma-separated list of privacy protection strength values, the order of which specifies the preference order. The three possible strength values are "low", "medium", and "high". A blank value will leave this setting unspecified. This setting will only be used by mechanisms which support it.

saslMutualAuthentication.description: Enable or disable mutual authentication. This setting will only be used by mechanisms which support it.

referral.description: Specifies how referrals are to be processed. There are three well-known values: "follow" (follow referrals automatically), "ignore" (ignore referrals), or "throw" (throw a ReferralException when a referral is encountered).

extraUserAttributes.description: A list of LDAP attributes to user property mappings that define additional user attributes to request from the LDAP server and to set on the user object.

attribute.description: The name used to look up the attribute in LDAP.

property.description: The property name that the attribute value will be stored under in the user object. If not provided, the attribute name will be used.

binary.description: Treat the LDAP attribute's value as a byte[] array instead of as a String.

multiValued.description: Treat the property as a multi-valued property instead of single-valued. The values will be retrievable on the user object as a list.

legacyNamingEnabled.description: If true, the user and role search base entries are parsed first as JNDI CompositeNames, and then the first element in each CompositeName is extracted and parsed as an LdapName (this is the default behavior in 8.1). If false, the user and role search base entries are parsed directly as LdapNames. Set this value to false unless you experience problems parsing the user and/or role search base entries as valid LdapNames.

datasource.description: The database connection this user source will use.

badgeAuthQuery.description:
A query that must return a row if the given badge provided is valid. The query will be run as a prepared statement, so use question mark (?) to represent the badge. The returned row must contain the username.
Example: SELECT username FROM USERS WHERE badge = ?

contactInfoQuery.description:
A query that returns all of the contact info for the user. The first column must be the contact type, the second column the contact value, and the third column the name of a schedule. Optional, may be blank.
Example: SELECT contact_type, contact_value, schedule FROM user_contact WHERE username=?

extraPropsQuery.description:
A query that returns name, value pairs of extra properties for the user. Will be run with one parameter: the username. Optional, may be blank.
Example: SELECT prop_name, prop_value FROM user_props WHERE username=?

findUserQuery.description:
A query that must return a row if a user with the given username exists. Only used if "List Users from Active Directory" is false. The query will be run as a prepared statement, so use question mark (?) to represent username. There must be at least one column: the username. Other columns are optional, supported columns are: [username, firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid]. If useruuid is present, it must be returned in all queries that support it.
Example: SELECT username, firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid FROM user_table WHERE username = ?

roleQuery.description:
A query that returns all possible roles that any user could be a member of. At least one column must be returned: the rolename. Other columns are optional, supported columns are: [rolename, roleuuid].
Example: SELECT rolename, roleuuid FROM roles

scheduleAdjustmentQuery.description:
A query that returns the upcoming schedule adjustments for the user. Columns must be Start(date), End(date), Available(boolean), Note(string). Optional, may be blank.
Example: SELECT start_date, end_date, is_available, note FROM user_schedule_adj WHERE username=?

userPropsQuery.description:
A query that returns the basic properties for a single user. Only used if "List Users from Active Directory" is true. Supported return columns are [firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge]. The username will be inserted into this query as a parameter.
Example: SELECT firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge FROM user_table WHERE username = ?

userQuery.description:
A query that returns a row containing each username. Only used if "List Users from Active Directory" is false. There must be at least one column: the username. Other columns are optional, supported columns are: [username, firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid]. If useruuid is present, it must be returned in all queries that support it.
Example: SELECT username, firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid FROM user_table

userRoleQuery.description:
A query that returns all of the roles that the provided user belongs to. The roles must be strings (i.e. the role names), and must be in the first column of the query's results. The username will be inserted into this query as a parameter.
Example: SELECT rolename FROM user_role_mapping WHERE username = ?

emailAttribute.description: The attribute name on the user object that represents the user's email address. Only used during initial user creation when populate users on-demand feature is enabled.

allowAnon.description:
If enabled, authentication attempts with blank passwords will be passed through to LDAP, which may choose to accept them.

WARNING: it is highly recommended to disable this setting unless you know it is required. AD servers may allow logging in as any user with a blank password when Security Authentication is set to “None” or “Simple” (even if a provided username does not exist in AD), which is a major security risk.

securityProtocol.description: The security protocol to use when connecting to the LDAP server. AUTO will attempt to use the most secure protocol available.

authenticationType.description: The authentication type to use when connecting to the LDAP server. AUTO will attempt to use the most secure authentication type available.

saslMechanism.description: An ordered list of space-separated mechanism names. The LDAP provider will use the first mechanism for which it finds an implementation. A blank value will leave this setting unspecified.

saslRealm.description: A realm defines the namespace from which the user is selected. A blank value will leave this setting unspecified. It is highly recommended to set the target realm otherwise any available realm may be chosen. This setting will only be used by mechanisms which support it.

saslQualityOfProtection.description: A comma-separated list of Quality-of-Protection (QoP) values, the order of which specifies the preference order. There are three well-known values: "auth" (authentication only), "auth-int" (authentication with integrity protection), and "auth-conf" (authentication with integrity and privacy protection). A blank value will leave this setting unspecified. This setting will only be used by mechanisms which support it.

saslProtectionStrength.description: A comma-separated list of privacy protection strength values, the order of which specifies the preference order. The three possible strength values are "low", "medium", and "high". A blank value will leave this setting unspecified. This setting will only be used by mechanisms which support it.

saslMutualAuthentication.description: Enable or disable mutual authentication. This setting will only be used by mechanisms which support it.

referral.description: Specifies how referrals are to be processed. There are three well-known values: "follow" (follow referrals automatically), "ignore" (ignore referrals), or "throw" (throw a ReferralException when a referral is encountered).

extraUserAttributes.description: A list of LDAP attributes to user property mappings that define additional user attributes to request from the LDAP server and to set on the user object.

attribute.description: The name used to look up the attribute in LDAP.

property.description: The property name that the attribute value will be stored under in the user object. If not provided, the attribute name will be used.

binary.description: Treat the LDAP attribute's value as a byte[] array instead of as a String.

multiValued.description: Treat the property as a multi-valued property instead of single-valued. The values will be retrievable on the user object as a list.

legacyNamingEnabled.description: If true, the user listing base entries are parsed first as JNDI CompositeNames, and then the first element in each CompositeName is extracted and parsed as an LdapName (this is the default behavior in 8.1). If false, the user listing base entries are parsed directly as LdapNames. Set this value to false unless you experience problems parsing the user listing base entries as valid LdapNames.

listUsersFromAD.description: If true, Active Directory will be queried for the list of all users. If false, users must be added manually.

populateUsersOnDemand.description: If true, a user record will be created in the Internal user source from the AD entry of any user who successfully authenticates into AD if the record does not already exist in the Internal user source at the time of authentication.

datasource.description: The database connection this user source will use.

badgeAuthQuery.description:
A query that must return a row if the given badge provided is valid. The query will be run as a prepared statement, so use question mark (?) to represent the badge. The returned row must contain the username.
Example: SELECT username FROM USERS WHERE badge = ?

contactInfoQuery.description:
A query that returns all of the contact info for the user. The first column must be the contact type, the second column the contact value, and the third column the name of a schedule. Optional, may be blank.
Example: SELECT contact_type, contact_value, schedule FROM user_contact WHERE username=?

extraPropsQuery.description:
A query that returns name, value pairs of extra properties for the user. Will be run with one parameter: the username. Optional, may be blank.
Example: SELECT prop_name, prop_value FROM user_props WHERE username=?

findUserQuery.description:
A query that must return a row if a user with the given username exists. Only used if "List Users from Active Directory" is false. The query will be run as a prepared statement, so use question mark (?) to represent username. There must be at least one column: the username. Other columns are optional, supported columns are: [username, firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid]. If useruuid is present, it must be returned in all queries that support it.
Example: SELECT username, firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid FROM user_table WHERE username = ?

roleQuery.description:
A query that returns all possible roles that any user could be a member of. At least one column must be returned: the rolename. Other columns are optional, supported columns are: [rolename, roleuuid].
Example: SELECT rolename, roleuuid FROM roles

scheduleAdjustmentQuery.description:
A query that returns the upcoming schedule adjustments for the user. Columns must be Start(date), End(date), Available(boolean), Note(string). Optional, may be blank.
Example: SELECT start_date, end_date, is_available, note FROM user_schedule_adj WHERE username=?

userPropsQuery.description:
A query that returns the basic properties for a single user. Only used if "List Users from Active Directory" is true. Supported return columns are [firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge]. The username will be inserted into this query as a parameter.
Example: SELECT firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge FROM user_table WHERE username = ?

userQuery.description:
A query that returns a row containing each username. Only used if "List Users from Active Directory" is false. There must be at least one column: the username. Other columns are optional, supported columns are: [username, firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid]. If useruuid is present, it must be returned in all queries that support it.
Example: SELECT username, firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid FROM user_table

userRoleQuery.description:
A query that returns all of the roles that the provided user belongs to. The roles must be strings (i.e. the role names), and must be in the first column of the query's results. The username will be inserted into this query as a parameter.
Example: SELECT rolename FROM user_role_mapping WHERE username = ?

authQuery.description:
A query that must return a row if the given username and password combination provided is valid. The query will be run as a prepared statement, so use question mark (?) to represent username first and then password. The returned row may contain the user's basic properties under the column names: [firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid]. If useruuid is present, it must be returned in all queries that support it.
Example: SELECT useruuid, firstname, lastname, schedule FROM USERS WHERE username = ? AND password = MD5(?)

badgeAuthQuery.description:
A query that must return a row if the given badge provided is valid. The query will be run as a prepared statement, so use question mark (?) to represent the badge. The returned row must contain the username and may contain the user's basic properties under the column names: [firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid]. If useruuid is present, it must be returned in all queries that support it.
Example: SELECT username, useruuid, firstname, lastname, schedule FROM USERS WHERE badge = ?

roleQuery.description:
A query that returns all possible roles that any user could be a member of. At least one column must be returned: the rolename. Other columns are optional, supported columns are: [rolename, roleuuid].
Example: SELECT rolename, roleuuid FROM roles

userRoleQuery.description:
A query that returns all of the roles that the provided user belongs to. The roles must be strings and must be in the first column of the query's results. The query will be run as a prepared statement with one parameter: the username.
Example: SELECT rolename FROM mapping_table WHERE username = ?

findUserQuery.description:
A query that must return a row if a user with the given username exists. The query will be run as a prepared statement, so use question mark (?) to represent username. There must be at least one column: the username. Other columns are optional, supported columns are: [username, firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid]. If useruuid is present, it must be returned in all queries that support it.
Example: SELECT username, useruuid, firstname, lastname, schedule, FROM USERS WHERE username = ?

userQuery.description:
A query that returns a row containing each username. There must be at least one column: the username. Other columns are optional, supported columns are: [username, firstname, lastname, schedule, language, notes, badge, useruuid]. If useruuid is present, it must be returned in all queries that support it.
Example: SELECT username, useruuid, firstname, lastname, schedule FROM USERS

contactInfoQuery.description:
A query that returns all of the contact info for the user. The first column must be the contact type, the second column the contact value. Optional, may be blank.
Example: SELECT contact_type, contact_value FROM user_contact WHERE username=?

scheduleAdjustmentQuery.description:
A query that returns the upcoming schedule adjustments for the user. Columns must be Start(date), End(date), Available(boolean), Note(string). Optional, may be blank.
Example: SELECT start_date, end_date, is_available, note FROM user_schedule_adj WHERE username=?

extraPropsQuery.description:
A query that returns name, value pairs of extra properties for the user. Will be run with one parameter: the username. Optional, may be blank.
Example: SELECT prop_name, prop_value FROM user_props WHERE username=?

enableUuids.description: When in automatic mode, UUIDs will be generated for user and role IDs.

cacheRetention.description: Number of days that the cache will retain recently used credentials.

passwordMaxAge.description: The maximum age (in days) that a password is valid for. A value of zero disables password expiration.

passwordMinLength.description: Passwords must be at least this many characters long.

passwordComplexity.description: The number of character types (lowercase letters, uppercase letters, digits, punctuation) each password must contain. For example, a value of 3 means passwords must have 3 of the 4 character types to be considered valid.

passwordHistory.description: The number of previous passwords to store. Passwords in the history list may not be re-used. A value of zero disables this feature.

passwordContainsPassword.description: If enabled, passwords may not contain any form of the word "password". This includes: password, pass, word, pwd, passwd and pword.

passwordContainsUserName.description: If enabled, passwords may not contain any form of the username.

passwordMaxRepeatedChars.description: The maximum number of consecutive repeated characters allowed in a password. Set to 0 to disable.

includeSchemaInTableName.description: In listing tables, the schema name will be included in order to create a fully-qualified name.

connectURL.description: The Connect URL is JDBC-driver specific. It usually contains the address of the machine that the database is running on.

username.description: The name of the user to authenticate with when connecting to the database.

type.title: Secret Type
type.description: The type of secret. Embedded secrets embed the encrypted secret within the configuration. Referenced secrets reference the secret in a secret provider.

data.title: Secret Data
data.description: The secret data. Embedded secrets are encrypted using JSON Web Encryption and encoded using the Flattened JWE JSON Serialization Syntax. Referenced secrets reference the secret using the secret provider and secret name pair.

protected.title: JWE Protected Header
protected.description: The base64-url-encoding of the UTF-8-encoded JWE Protected Header.

encrypted_key.title: JWE Encrypted Key
encrypted_key.description: The base64-url-encoding of the JWE Encrypted Key.

iv.title: JWE Initialization Vector
iv.description: The base64-url-encoding of the JWE Initialization Vector.

ciphertext.title: JWE Ciphertext
ciphertext.description: The base64-url-encoding of the JWE Ciphertext.

tag.title: JWE Authentication Tag
tag.description: The base64-url-encoding of the JWE Authentication Tag.

type.title: Secret Type
type.description: The type of secret. Embedded secrets embed the encrypted secret within the configuration. Referenced secrets reference the secret in a secret provider.

data.title: Secret Data
data.description: The secret data. Embedded secrets are encrypted using JSON Web Encryption and encoded using the Flattened JWE JSON Serialization Syntax. Referenced secrets reference the secret using the secret provider and secret name pair.

providerName.title: Secret Provider Name
providerName.description: The name of the secret provider.

password.description: The password of the user to authenticate with when connecting to the database.

connectionResetParams.description: A set of commands (one per line) that will be executed each time a connection is pulled from the pool. Can be used to reset environment variables.

defaultTransactionLevel.description: The isolation level to use for each connection.

poolInitSize.description: The initial number of connections that are created when the pool is started.

poolMaxActive.description: The maximum number of active connections that can be allocated from this pool at the same time, or negative for no limit.

poolMaxIdle.description: The maximum number of connections that can remain idle in the pool, without extra ones being released, or negative for no limit.

poolMinIdle.description: The minimum number of connections that can remain idle in the pool, without extra ones being created, or zero to create none.

poolMaxWait.description: The maximum number of milliseconds that the pool will wait (when there are no available connections) for a connection to be returned before throwing an exception, or -1 to wait indefinitely.

validationQuery.description: A SQL query that will be used to validate connections from the pool. This query MUST be an SQL SELECT statement that returns at least one row.

testOnBorrow.description: When true, connections will be validated before being borrowed from the pool. If the connection fails to validate, it will be dropped from the pool, and we will attempt to borrow another.

testOnReturn.description: When true, connections will be validated before being returned to the pool.

testWhileIdle.description: When true, connections will be validated by the idle connection evictor. If a connection fails to validate, it will be dropped from the pool.

evictionRate.description: The number of milliseconds to sleep between runs of the idle connection evictor thread. When non-positive, no idle connection evictor thread will be run.

evictionTests.description: The number of connections to examine during each run of the idle object evictor thread (if any).

accessTokenTimeout.description: Amount of time in seconds to wait for a valid access token before giving up on sending an email. refreshBeforeExpiration.description: The amount of time in seconds before an access token expires when a new token should be requested. Values less than or equal to zero results in new access token requests exactly when the last access token expires.

collection.description: The config collection to modify the resource in

enabled.description: Whether the resource should be enabled

requireSSL.description: If true, only connections that use SSL to encrypt traffic will be allowed. This setting only applies to incoming connections.

requireTwoWayAuth.description: Enforces two-way SSL authentication. If true, you will need to install the remote machine's certificate on this machine, in addition to manual approval of this machine's certificate on the remote machine.

receiveQueueMax.description: DEPRECATED: This property has been superceded by the dataChannelQueueSize property and the dataChannelThreadPoolMax property, and is no longer used internally.

overloadWaitSecs.description: DEPRECATED: This property is no longer used within the gateway network system.

allowIncoming.description: If false, only outward connections defined on this gateway will be allowed.

securityPolicy.description: Dictates what connections are allowed. If set to 'Approved', incoming connections must be approved from the Incoming Connections page.

whitelist.description: If connection policy is set to Specified List, this is the comma-separated list of ${GATEWAY} names which will be allowed to connect.

allowedProxyHops.description: The maximum number of proxy hops which could be used to reach the destination Gateway. Any number less than or equal to zero is equivalent to no proxy hops allowed.

websocketSessionIdleTimeout.description: The maximum number of milliseconds that a websocket is allowed to remain idle before it is closed. This value should always be set higher than outgoing connection ping rates to avoid premature connection termination.

tempFilesMaxAgeHours.description: The maximum number of hours that a gateway network temporary file will be retained. Files older than this value will be purged. Set to 0 to disable cleaning of temporary files.

incomingPingRateMillis.description: How often, in milliseconds, to send a ping to a remote machine. This will allow an incoming connection's health to be monitored. Set to 0 to disable pings sent from an incoming connection.

incomingPingTimeoutMillis.description: The maximum time, in milliseconds, allowed for a ping response. Pings that time out are counted as missed pings.

incomingPingMaxMissed.description: The amount of missed pings that will force an incoming connection to be considered faulted.

proxyInterceptServiceCalls.description: If enabled on a proxy gateway, this setting will intercept recurring service enumeration calls that the proxy gateway normally passes along. If the proxy gateway already has the service enumeration information available locally, then that information is returned directly instead of forwarding the call. dataChannelThreadPoolMaxSize.description: The maximum number of threads that can be created by the data channel thread pool. This thread pool is used to process incoming messages.

x5u.title: X.509 URL
x5u.description: The "x5u" (X.509 URL) parameter is a URI [RFC3986] that refers to a resource for an X.509 public key certificate or certificate chain [RFC5280]. The identified resource MUST provide a representation of the certificate or certificate chain that conforms to RFC 5280 in PEM-encoded form, with each certificate delimited as specified in Section 6.1 of RFC 4945. The key in the first certificate MUST match the public key represented by other members of the JWK.

x5c.title: X.509 Certificate Chain
x5c.description: The "x5c" (X.509 certificate chain) parameter contains a chain of one or more PKIX certificates [RFC5280]. The certificate chain is represented as a JSON array of certificate value strings. Each string in the array is a base64-encoded (Section 4 of [RFC4648] -- not base64url-encoded) DER [ITU.X690.1994] PKIX certificate value.The PKIX certificate containing the key value MUST be the first certificate. This MAY be followed by additional certificates, with each subsequent certificate being the one used to certify the previous one. The key in the first certificate MUST match the public key represented by other members of the JWK.

x5t.title: X.509 Certificate SHA-1 Thumbprint
x5t.description: The "x5t" (X.509 certificate SHA-1 thumbprint) parameter is a base64url-encoded SHA-1 thumbprint (a.k.a. digest) of the DER encoding of an X.509 certificate [RFC5280]. The key in the certificate MUST match the public key represented by other members of the JWK.

x5t#S256.title: X.509 Certificate SHA-256 Thumbprint

allowedIdTokenSigningAlgorithms.title: Allowed ID Token Signing Algorithms
allowedIdTokenSigningAlgorithms.description: The list of JWS algorithms that Ignition will allow the OP to use for signing ID tokens. Warning: allowing a value of "none" could allow a malicious user to forge ID tokens, and Ignition will be unable to distinguish between an authentic ID token issued by the OP and a forged ID token issued by the malicious user. Therefore, it is recommended never to allow "none".

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: A list of default scopes which will be sent for each authorization request to the OP.

httpPostLogoutEnabled.title: Logout using HTTP POST
httpPostLogoutEnabled.description: If true, users will be redirected to the Logout URL using HTTP POST. If false, users will be redirected to the Logout URL using HTTP GET. HTTP GET is generally less secure since potentially sensitive data could be leaked in URL query parameters. HTTP GET requests are limited in the size of URL query parameters it can support, whereas HTTP POST requests generally have no such limit.

spEntityId.title: SP Entity ID
spEntityId.description: The Service Provider's Entity ID. In this case, the Service Provider is the current Ignition Gateway.

spEntityIdEnabled.title: Enable SP Entity ID
spEntityIdEnabled.description: True if the SP Entity ID setting should be used. False to automatically generate the SP Entity ID based on the hostname that the client uses to connect to this Gateway.

acsBinding.title: ACS Binding
acsBinding.description: The expected binding used by the Identity Provider when interacting with Ignition's Assertion Consumer Service.

nameIdFormat.title: Name ID Format
nameIdFormat.description: The expected name ID format for subjects of assertions resulting from Authn Requests.

ssoServiceConfig.title: SSO Service Config
ssoServiceConfig.description: The Identity Provider's Single Sign-On (SSO) Service Configuration.

forceAuthnEnabled.title: Force Authn
forceAuthnEnabled.description: Setting this value to true will force complying Identity Providers to authenticate the user each time instead of relying on a previous security context. See section 3.4.1 of saml-core-2.0-os for more details.

responseSignaturesRequired.title: Require Response Signatures
responseSignaturesRequired.description: If true, the Gateway will require each Identity Provider Response to have a valid signature. Warning: if both this value and the 'Require Assertion Signatures' value is set to false, malicious users may trivially compromise the security of your Gateway by forging Responses and/or Assertions. It is recommended to have at least one of these two settings set to true depending on whether the IdP signs Responses, Assertions, or both.

assertionSignaturesRequired.title: Require Assertion Signatures
assertionSignaturesRequired.description: If true, the Gateway will require each Identity Provider Assertion to have a valid signature. Warning: if both this value and the 'Require Response Signatures' value is set to false, malicious users may trivially compromise the security of your Gateway by forging Responses and/or Assertions. It is recommended to have at least one of these two settings set to true depending on whether the IdP signs Responses, Assertions, or both.

idpMetadataUrl.title: IdP Metadata URL
idpMetadataUrl.description: URL to the SAML Identity Provider Metadata document.

idpMetadataUrlEnabled.title: Enable IdP Metadata URL
idpMetadataUrlEnabled.description: If true, and if the IdP Metadata URL is specified, the Identity Provider's signature verifying keys and certificates will be automatically downloaded from IdP metadata URL. New keys and certificates will be automatically fetched when the Identity Provider generates them. If unchecked, then the static set of keys and certificates embedded in this configuration are used, so when the identity provider rotates them, they must be manually added to this configuration.

signatureVerifyingCertificates.description: An array of signing certificates that Ignition uses to validate signatures from the IdP. Each array entry is a base64-encoded DER-encoding of an X.509 key.

use.title: Key Use
use.description: The "use" (public key use) parameter identifies the intended use of the public key. The "use" parameter is employed to indicate whether a public key is used for encrypting data or verifying the signature on data.

key_ops.title: Key Operations
key_ops.description: The "key_ops" (key operations) parameter identifies the operation(s) for which the key is intended to be used.

alg.title: Algorithm
alg.description: The "alg" (algorithm) parameter identifies the algorithm intended for use with the key.

kid.title: Key ID
kid.description: The "kid" (key ID) parameter is used to match a specific key.

x5u.title: X.509 URL
x5u.description: The "x5u" (X.509 URL) parameter is a URI [RFC3986] that refers to a resource for an X.509 public key certificate or certificate chain [RFC5280]. The identified resource MUST provide a representation of the certificate or certificate chain that conforms to RFC 5280 in PEM-encoded form, with each certificate delimited as specified in Section 6.1 of RFC 4945. The key in the first certificate MUST match the public key represented by other members of the JWK.

x5c.title: X.509 Certificate Chain
x5c.description: The "x5c" (X.509 certificate chain) parameter contains a chain of one or more PKIX certificates [RFC5280]. The certificate chain is represented as a JSON array of certificate value strings. Each string in the array is a base64-encoded (Section 4 of [RFC4648] -- not base64url-encoded) DER [ITU.X690.1994] PKIX certificate value.The PKIX certificate containing the key value MUST be the first certificate. This MAY be followed by additional certificates, with each subsequent certificate being the one used to certify the previous one. The key in the first certificate MUST match the public key represented by other members of the JWK.

x5t.title: X.509 Certificate SHA-1 Thumbprint
x5t.description: The "x5t" (X.509 certificate SHA-1 thumbprint) parameter is a base64url-encoded SHA-1 thumbprint (a.k.a. digest) of the DER encoding of an X.509 certificate [RFC5280]. The key in the certificate MUST match the public key represented by other members of the JWK.

x5t#S256.title: X.509 Certificate SHA-256 Thumbprint
x5t#S256.description: The "x5t#S256" (X.509 certificate SHA-256 thumbprint) parameter is a base64url-encoded SHA-256 thumbprint (a.k.a. digest) of the DER encoding of an X.509 certificate [RFC5280]. The key in the certificate MUST match the public key represented by other members of the JWK.

allowedIdTokenSigningAlgorithms.title: Allowed ID Token Signing Algorithms
allowedIdTokenSigningAlgorithms.description: The list of JWS algorithms that Ignition will allow the OP to use for signing ID tokens. Warning: allowing a value of "none" could allow a malicious user to forge ID tokens, and Ignition will be unable to distinguish between an authentic ID token issued by the OP and a forged ID token issued by the malicious user. Therefore, it is recommended never to allow "none".

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: A list of default scopes which will be sent for each authorization request to the OP.

httpPostLogoutEnabled.title: Logout using HTTP POST
httpPostLogoutEnabled.description: If true, users will be redirected to the Logout URL using HTTP POST. If false, users will be redirected to the Logout URL using HTTP GET. HTTP GET is generally less secure since potentially sensitive data could be leaked in URL query parameters. HTTP GET requests are limited in the size of URL query parameters it can support, whereas HTTP POST requests generally have no such limit.

spEntityId.title: SP Entity ID
spEntityId.description: The Service Provider's Entity ID. In this case, the Service Provider is the current Ignition Gateway.

spEntityIdEnabled.title: Enable SP Entity ID
spEntityIdEnabled.description: True if the SP Entity ID setting should be used. False to automatically generate the SP Entity ID based on the hostname that the client uses to connect to this Gateway.

acsBinding.title: ACS Binding
acsBinding.description: The expected binding used by the Identity Provider when interacting with Ignition's Assertion Consumer Service.

nameIdFormat.title: Name ID Format
nameIdFormat.description: The expected name ID format for subjects of assertions resulting from Authn Requests.

ssoServiceConfig.title: SSO Service Config
ssoServiceConfig.description: The Identity Provider's Single Sign-On (SSO) Service Configuration.

forceAuthnEnabled.title: Force Authn
forceAuthnEnabled.description: Setting this value to true will force complying Identity Providers to authenticate the user each time instead of relying on a previous security context. See section 3.4.1 of saml-core-2.0-os for more details.

responseSignaturesRequired.title: Require Response Signatures
responseSignaturesRequired.description: If true, the Gateway will require each Identity Provider Response to have a valid signature. Warning: if both this value and the 'Require Assertion Signatures' value is set to false, malicious users may trivially compromise the security of your Gateway by forging Responses and/or Assertions. It is recommended to have at least one of these two settings set to true depending on whether the IdP signs Responses, Assertions, or both.

assertionSignaturesRequired.title: Require Assertion Signatures
assertionSignaturesRequired.description: If true, the Gateway will require each Identity Provider Assertion to have a valid signature. Warning: if both this value and the 'Require Response Signatures' value is set to false, malicious users may trivially compromise the security of your Gateway by forging Responses and/or Assertions. It is recommended to have at least one of these two settings set to true depending on whether the IdP signs Responses, Assertions, or both.

idpMetadataUrl.title: IdP Metadata URL
idpMetadataUrl.description: URL to the SAML Identity Provider Metadata document.

idpMetadataUrlEnabled.title: Enable IdP Metadata URL
idpMetadataUrlEnabled.description: If true, and if the IdP Metadata URL is specified, the Identity Provider's signature verifying keys and certificates will be automatically downloaded from IdP metadata URL. New keys and certificates will be automatically fetched when the Identity Provider generates them. If unchecked, then the static set of keys and certificates embedded in this configuration are used, so when the identity provider rotates them, they must be manually added to this configuration.

signatureVerifyingCertificates.description: An array of signing certificates that Ignition uses to validate signatures from the IdP. Each array entry is a base64-encoded DER-encoding of an X.509 key.

secretRequired.description: If set to true, the user will be required to provide a secret in addition to their badge scan. If false, the user will only need to scan their badge to successfully authenticate.

sessionInactivityTimeout.title: Session Inactivity Timeout
sessionInactivityTimeout.description: The number of minutes which must elapse before expiring a session due to user inactivity. Sessions will not timeout if set to any number less than or equal to zero.

sessionExp.title: Session Expiration
sessionExp.description: The maximum number of minutes a session may exist before it is expired. Sessions will not have a max lifetime if set to any number less than or equal to zero.

rememberMeExp.title: Remember Me Expiration
rememberMeExp.description: The maximum number of hours a user will be remembered if they elect to be remembered. Remember Me is disabled when this value is set to any number less than or equal to zero.

type.description: The type of secret. Embedded secrets embed the encrypted secret within the configuration. Referenced secrets reference the secret in a secret provider.

data.title: Secret Data
data.description: The secret data. Embedded secrets are encrypted using JSON Web Encryption and encoded using the Flattened JWE JSON Serialization Syntax. Referenced secrets reference the secret using the secret provider and secret name pair.

type.title: Secret Type
type.description: The type of secret. Embedded secrets embed the encrypted secret within the configuration. Referenced secrets reference the secret in a secret provider.

data.title: Secret Data
data.description: The secret data. Embedded secrets are encrypted using JSON Web Encryption and encoded using the Flattened JWE JSON Serialization Syntax. Referenced secrets reference the secret using the secret provider and secret name pair.

providerName.title: Secret Provider Name
providerName.description: The name of the secret provider.

authorizationUrl.title: Authorization URL
authorizationUrl.description: Optional URL of the authorization server's OAuth 2.0 Authorization Endpoint.

authorizationResponseMode.title: Authorization Response Mode
authorizationResponseMode.description: The authorization response mode that Ignition will request from the authorization server on each authorization request. If unset, Ignition will not encode the response mode parameter on authorization requests, which should default the response mode to "query".

tokenUrl.title: Token URL
tokenUrl.description: Required URL of the authorization server's OAuth 2.0 Token Endpoint.

httpVersion.title: HTTP Version
httpVersion.description: The maximum HTTP version supported by the authorization server's token endpoint. The Gateway's HTTP client will use this version when making HTTP requests to the authorization server.

httpConnectTimeout.title: HTTP Connect Timeout
httpConnectTimeout.description: In the case where the Gateway's HTTP client needs to establish a new HTTP connection with the authorization server, if the connection cannot be established within the given amount of time in milliseconds, then the connection attempt and any pending request requiring the connection will time out. There will be no timeout if the value is less than or equal to zero (the Gateway will wait forever for the connection to be made).

httpRequestTimeout.title: HTTP Request Timeout
httpRequestTimeout.description: The timeout in milliseconds for each HTTP request sent from the Gateway's HTTP client to the authorization server. If an HTTP response is not received within the specified timeout after sending an HTTP request then the HTTP request will time out. There will be no timeout if the value is less than or equal to zero (the Gateway will wait forever for a response).
